steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Wash 500g chicken thoroughly. Marinate with 1/2 cup smoothly beaten thick yogurt, 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp biryani masala, 1 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp red chili powder, juice of 1/2 lemon, and 1 tsp salt. Mix thoroughly and refrigerate for at least 1 to 2 hours for softening.

Step 2 (Marinate / Mix): Wash 2 cups aged Basmati rice gently under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak in plenty of water for 30 minutes. In a large pot, bring 8 cups of water to a fast boil with whole spices (2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 2 green cardamoms, 1-inch cinnamon stick) and 1 tbsp salt.

Step 3 (Cook on Low Heat): Add the soaked, drained rice to boiling water and cook uncovered on high flame for exactly 5-6 minutes until 70% cooked (the grain should break into 3 pieces when pressed between fingers). Drain immediately in a strainer.

Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Heat 3 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp ghee in a wide heavy-bottomed cooking pot or biryani pot. Fry 2 thinly sliced large onions on medium heat with a pinch of salt until deep golden brown and crispy. Remove half the fried onions and set aside for layering.

Step 5 (Fry Onions & Spices): In the same pot with remaining onions, add the marinated chicken along with 3 slit green chilies and half of chopped mint and coriander leaves. Cook on high heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring continuously until the chicken is sealed and releases its juices.

Step 6 (Fry Onions & Spices): Lower flame to minimum. Evenly spread the chicken at the bottom. Layer the 70% cooked flavorful rice on top of the chicken. Scatter the reserved golden fried onions, fresh chopped mint leaves, coriander, 2 tbsp saffron-infused warm milk, and 1 tbsp melted ghee across the rice layer.

Step 7 (Cook on Low Heat): Seal the pot tightly with aluminum foil or kneaded wheat dough, then place a heavy lid on top. Cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes (or place the pot on a preheated heavy iron tawa on low flame to prevent burning).

Step 8 (Finish & Serve): Turn off heat and allow the biryani to rest without stirring for 10 minutes. Gently fluff with a flat spoon from the bottom up to mix layers without breaking rice grains. Serve piping hot with onion-cucumber raita and Mirchi ka Salan.

Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Clean 500g mutton thoroughly. In a pressure cooker, add mutton, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, and 1/2 cup water. cook in pressure cooker on medium flame for 5-6 cooker whistles until meat is 80% tender and soft and juicy.

Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Pick 2 large bunches of red-stem gongura (sorrel) leaves, wash thoroughly, and drain. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, add the leaves with 4 slit green chilies and a splash of water. Cook on low-medium flame for 5-6 minutes until leaves wilt and turn soft. Coarsely mash using a wooden pestle or pulse in a blender for 2 seconds.

Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and a sprig of fresh curry leaves. When they crackle, add 2 finely chopped medium onions and saute until soft and pink and golden.

Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and saute for 1 minute until raw aroma goes away. Add 2 chopped tomatoes, 1.5 tbsp spicy Andhra red chili powder, 1 tbsp coriander powder, and 1/2 tsp garam masala. Cook on medium heat until tomatoes break down and oil separates from the edges.

Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour in the cooked mutton along with its rich broth. Bring to a boil and cook on low heat for 6-8 minutes on medium flame. Stir in the mashed gongura paste, mixing thoroughly to blend the sour and savory notes.

Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Cover and cook on low heat on low heat for 10-12 minutes until gravy turns thick and dark, and meat absorbs the tangy flavor. In a small ladle, heat 1 tsp ghee with 2 crushed garlic cloves and dried red chilies, pour over the curry, and serve hot with steamed rice and ghee.

Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Peel, clean the black thread from, and thoroughly clean 400g fresh medium prawns. Toss with 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1 tsp lemon juice; let sit for 10 minutes to eliminate any raw odor.

Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat 2.5 tbsp peanut oil in a thick pan on medium flame. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and 10 fresh curry leaves. Add 2 finely chopped large onions and saute until light golden brown.

Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Stir in 1.5 tbsp freshly ground ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chilies; saute for 90 seconds until fragrant. Add 2 finely chopped ripe tomatoes and cook until soft and oil begins to glisten.

Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1.5 tbsp Andhra red chili powder, 1 tbsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin powder, and salt to taste. Saute the spices on low flame for 1 minute without burning.

Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Add the marinated prawns into the masala. Toss on medium-high heat for 3 minutes until prawns curl into 'C' shapes and release natural juices. Pour in 1/2 cup warm water, cover, and cook on low heat on medium-low heat for 6-8 minutes (do not overcook prawns to keep them tender and juicy).

Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Remove lid and cook on medium flame until gravy thickens into a glossy semi-dry curry (iguru). top with fresh freshly chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice.

Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Clean 500g freshwater fish steaks (Rohu or Katla) with crystal salt and turmeric; rinse and drain. Soak a lemon-sized ball of aged tamarind in 1.5 cups warm water for 15 minutes and extract thick, smooth pulp.

Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat 3 tbsp sesame (gingelly) oil in an earthen clay pot (chatti) on medium flame. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds (methi), and a generous sprig of curry leaves. Allow seeds to splutter without burning.
Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1.5 cups finely sliced small shallots (sambar onions) and 4 slit green chilies. Saute on medium flame until onions turn soft and soft and pink.

Step 4 (Cook on Low Heat): Add 2 chopped country tomatoes, 1.5 tbsp spicy red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander powder, and crystal salt. Pour in the tamarind extract along with 1 cup water. Bring the gravy to a vigorous fast boil for 8-10 minutes until the raw tamarind smell disappears.

Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Lower flame to medium. Gently slide fish slices into the boiling gravy in a single layer. Hold the pot by its handles and swirl gently to coat fish (do not stir vigorously with a ladle to avoid breaking fish).

Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Cover partially and cook on low heat on low-medium heat for 12-15 minutes until fish is cooked and oil floats on the surface. Turn off heat. For authentic taste, let the curry rest for at least 3-4 hours before serving with hot rice.

Step 1 (Preparation): Boil 5 large eggs in salted water for 10 minutes until hard-boiled. Cool in ice water, peel shells, and make 3 vertical slits on each egg. Heat 1 tsp oil with a pinch of turmeric and chili powder in a pan; roll the boiled eggs for 2 minutes until outer skin is blistered and golden.

Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat 2 tbsp oil in a saucepan. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and 8 fresh curry leaves. Add 2 finely chopped medium onions and 2 slit green chilies; saute until golden brown.

Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and saute for 1 minute. Add 2 pureed ripe tomatoes, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, and 1/2 tsp garam masala. Cook on medium heat until oil releases from sides.
Step 4 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour in 3/4 cup warm water and season with salt. Bring gravy to a gentle cook on low heat. Add the blistered boiled eggs into the gravy.

Step 5 (Finish & Serve): Cover and cook on low heat on low flame for 6-8 minutes so the eggs absorb the rich masala. top with chopped cilantro and serve hot with steamed basmati rice, chapati, or parotta.
Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Wash and clean the meat/seafood thoroughly. Marinate with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, and salt for 30 minutes.
Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat oil/ghee in a heavy pot or pressure cooker. Add whole spices, curry leaves, and sliced onions; saute until golden brown.
Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add ginger-garlic paste, pureed tomatoes, red chili powder, coriander powder, and garam masala; saute until oil glistens on the edges.
Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add the marinated meat and saute on medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes until seared.
Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Add measured water, cover with lid, and cook in pressure cooker (or slow cook on low heat) until meat is fork-tender and soft and juicy.
Step 6 (Cook on Low Heat): Open lid and cook on low heat for 3-5 minutes until gravy reaches desired thick, glossy thickness.
Step 7 (Finish & Serve): top with fresh chopped coriander and serve hot with steamed basmati rice, Ragi Sankati, or soft rotis.

steps: Step 1 (Marinate & Roast Eggs): Boil 4 eggs, peel, make shallow slits, and roll in a pinch of turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Shallow fry in 1 tbsp ghee for 2 minutes until golden blistered.
Step 2 (Whole Spices Tadka): In a pressure cooker or heavy pot, heat 1 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp oil. Sizzle bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, and star anise until aromatic.
Step 3 (Saute Base): Add sliced onions, slit green chilies, and curry leaves; saute until onions turn translucent golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and chopped tomatoes, cooking until oil separates.
Step 4 (Simmer Rice & Eggs): Add washed and drained basmati rice, turmeric, garam masala, and 2 cups water (per 1 cup rice). Gently place the fried eggs in the pot. Season with salt.
Step 5 (Cook & Serve): Cover and pressure cook for 2 whistles on medium flame (or simmer on low heat covered for 15 minutes). Rest 5 minutes, fluff gently, and garnish with chopped fresh coriander.

Step 1 (Cook Dal): Wash toor dal and masoor dal thoroughly. Pressure cook with 3 cups water, turmeric, and 1/2 tsp salt for 4 whistles until soft and mushy. Whisk smooth.
Step 2 (Fry Base): Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds and mustard seeds until they splutter. Saute onions and green chilies until golden brown.
Step 3 (Add Aromatics): Stir in ginger-garlic paste and diced tomatoes. Cook on medium heat until tomatoes turn soft and pulpy.
Step 4 (Simmer): Pour the cooked dal into the masala pan, adjusting water for desired consistency. Simmer for 5 minutes, adding crushed kasuri methi and salt.
Step 5 (Garnish): Finish with chopped fresh coriander leaves and a dollop of pure ghee on top. Serve hot with steamed basmati rice or rotis.

ingredients: cooked rice (chilled basmati or long grain)
steps: Step 1 (Prep Ingredients): Use cold, pre-cooked day-old rice to ensure separate, fluffy grains. Finely mince garlic, slit green chilies, and chop carrots and spring onions.

Step 2 (Scramble Eggs): Beat 3 eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt and crushed black pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a smoking-hot wok or wide pan, pour in eggs, and scramble softly until 80% set. Remove and set aside.

Step 3 (Stir-Fry Aromatics): In the same hot wok, add 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry minced garlic and green chilies on high heat for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add diced carrots and beans; toss for 2 minutes to retain crunch.

Step 4 (Toss Rice & Seasoning): Add the chilled cooked rice and scrambled eggs into the wok. Drizzle 1 tbsp soy sauce, freshly cracked black pepper, and salt across the sides. Toss continuously on high flame for 3 minutes.
Step 5 (Garnish & Serve): Fold in freshly chopped spring onion greens, toss for 30 seconds, and transfer to a serving bowl. Enjoy hot with chili vinegar or spicy schezwan sauce.
Step 1 (Cook & Mash Rice): Cook rice slightly soft with a little extra water. Mash the warm rice gently with the back of a ladle. Let it cool to lukewarm.
Step 2 (Mix Curd & Milk): Add smooth beaten fresh curd, warm milk, and salt to the mashed rice. Mix thoroughly until creamy and luscious.
Step 3 (Temple Tempering): Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a small tadka pan. Add mustard seeds, urad dal, and chana dal until golden. Add slit green chilies, grated ginger, curry leaves, and a pinch of hing.
Step 4 (Combine): Pour the sizzling tempering directly into the creamy curd rice. Fold gently to distribute the crunchy dals and aromatics evenly.
Step 5 (Garnish & Serve): Garnish with golden roasted cashews and vibrant pomegranate pearls. Serve slightly chilled or at room temperature with lemon pickle.

Soak whole green gram and raw rice in water for 4 to 6 hours or overnight.
Grind the drained soaked gram with fresh ginger, green chillies, cumin seeds, and salt into a smooth, thick batter.
Heat a cast-iron tawa or griddle, pour a ladleful of batter, and spread quickly into a thin, crispy crepe.
Sprinkle finely chopped onions, drizzle ghee or oil around the edges, and roast until golden and crisp on both sides.
Serve hot with spicy ginger chutney (allam pachadi) or upma.
Step 1 (Preparation): Prepare or ferment the batter/grains with water and salt as specified to achieve the ideal smooth, pourable thickness.
Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat oil/ghee in a pan or griddle. Saute mustard seeds, ginger, green chilies, curry leaves, and chopped onions until fragrant.
Step 3 (Cook on Low Heat): Spread the batter thinly on a well-seasoned hot cast-iron tawa (or stream grains into boiling seasoned water for upma/pongal).
Step 4 (Cook on Low Heat): Drizzle oil/ghee along edges and cook on medium flame until golden brown, crispy on the edges, and cooked through in the center.
Step 5 (Step 5): Flip or fold gently when bottom turns golden and releases easily from the pan.
Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Serve hot right off the stove with traditional Allam Pachadi (ginger chutney), coconut chutney, and piping hot Sambar.
Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Rinse toor dal / moong dal thoroughly in cold water until water runs clear. Soak for 20 minutes for quick, even cooking.

Step 2 (Marinate / Mix): In a pressure cooker, add soaked lentils, chopped vegetables/greens, green chilies, tomatoes, turmeric, and 2.5 cups of water. cook in pressure cooker on medium flame for 3 to 4 cooker whistles until soft and mushy.
Step 3 (Step 3): Allow pressure to release naturally. Open lid, add crystal salt, and mash the dal gently using a wooden masher (pappu gutti) to a creamy thickness.

Step 4 (Add Tadka (Popu)): In a small pan, heat 1.5 tbsp ghee or oil on medium flame. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, crushed garlic cloves, dry red chilies, and a sprig of fresh curry leaves until fragrant.
Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour the sizzling tempering directly into the mashed dal. Cover immediately with a lid for 2 minutes to trap the aroma, then cook on low heat on low for 3 minutes.
Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Serve piping hot poured over steamed white rice with a dollop of pure homemade ghee and spicy Andhra pickle or vadiyalu.

recipe_name: Murgh Kali Mirch (Black Pepper Chicken Curry)
steps: Step 1 (Marinate Chicken): Toss 500g chicken with 1/2 cup thick beaten yogurt, 1 tbsp crushed black pepper, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, and 1 tsp salt. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Step 2 (Aromatics Base): Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a deep pan. Sizzle green cardamoms and cloves. Add boiled onion paste and cook on medium heat until water evaporates and paste turns lightly golden.
Step 3 (Cook Chicken): Add marinated chicken and slit green chilies. Sear on high heat for 6-8 minutes until chicken seals and turns opaque.
Step 4 (Simmer Creamy Gravy): Stir in cashew paste and 1/2 cup warm water. Cover with lid and cook on low flame for 15 minutes until chicken is tender and succulent.
Step 5 (Finish with Pepper): Stir in 2 tbsp fresh cream, 1 tsp freshly crushed black pepper, and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer for 2 minutes and serve warm with butter naan or steamed basmati rice.

Step 1 (Boil Chana with Tea Bag): Soak kabuli chana overnight (8 hours). Pressure cook with 1 black tea bag, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, salt, and water for 6-7 whistles until completely tender and naturally dark.

Step 2 (Spice Coating): Discard tea bag. Drain water (reserve 1 cup). Place hot boiled chana in a bowl and sprinkle chole masala, anardana powder, amchur powder, and red chili powder evenly over them.
Step 3 (Sizzling Tadka): Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan until smoking hot. Add cumin seeds, ginger juliennes, and slit green chilies. Pour sizzling ghee directly over the spiced chana.

Step 4 (Simmer): Transfer back into a pot, add reserved cooking broth, and gently mash a small portion of chickpeas to thicken the rustic gravy. Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes until flavors infuse.
Step 5 (Serve): Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro, pickled ginger, and sliced onions. Pair with fluffy bhature or piping hot puris.

recipe_name: Dondakaya Vepudu (Tindora / Ivy Gourd Fry with Peanuts)
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Wash, peel, and chop the vegetables into uniform pieces to ensure even cooking and browning.
Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan on medium heat. Add mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, and curry leaves; saute until dals turn golden.
Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add the chopped vegetables, green chilies, turmeric, and salt. Saute uncovered on medium-low flame, stirring every 2-3 minutes.
Step 4 (Step 4): Continue roasting for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender on the inside and lightly crisped and browned on the edges.
Step 5 (Step 5): Sprinkle roasted peanut powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, or fresh finely shredded coconut as specified in ingredients.
Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Toss for 2 minutes on medium flame until spices coat the vegetables evenly. Serve hot as a crispy side dish with Sambar, Rasam, or Dal.

steps: Step 1 (Preparation): Prepare or ferment the batter/grains with water and salt as specified to achieve the ideal smooth, pourable thickness.
Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat oil/ghee in a pan or griddle. Saute mustard seeds, ginger, green chilies, curry leaves, and chopped onions until fragrant.
Step 3 (Cook on Low Heat): Spread the batter thinly on a well-seasoned hot cast-iron tawa (or stream grains into boiling seasoned water for upma/pongal).
